Subject: Initial pass on output ownership & training language

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, attaching ACME's redline of the MSA + Order Form (ACME_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx). Two narrow items we want to surface so they don't get lost in the doc:

1) Output ownership: ACME asked for an explicit assignment of output/title for model-generated content where they supply input data. We typically grant a broad customer right to use outputs but do not assign title for preexisting Redwood models or datasets.

2) Training / model reuse: ACME is requesting a clause that allows them to opt in to training (and for Redwood to retain a license to use their data for model training). They want a perpetual, royalty-free license to incorporate outputs back into their models (and for Redwood to use customer content for training unless they opt out).

Can you confirm ACME's priority between downstream assignment (title) vs. the right to opt-in for training? That will help us propose a compromise that keeps their productization needs intact while protecting Redwood's model IP and safety guardrails.

Next steps I propose: we send a short summary with 2 options (Customer-assigned title limited to customer-created artifacts OR standard use-rights + enhanced attribution & telemetry controls), and ask ACME to pick.

Thanks — I copied Karthik and Marissa for legal/product alignment.

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the redline. For ACME the priority is:

- Clear title/ownership to outputs that are generated from our proprietary inputs and prompts. We need that for downstream licensing to our customers.
- Separate, negotiable permission for Redwood to use ACME data for training. That permission is a gating point for us — we can opt in, but only after formal approval and with controls (anonymization, limited retention, and an agreed scope).

I attach a short internal note summarizing the ask; legal will need a proposed Redwood position before we escalate to procurement.

Thanks,

Sarah / ACME team —

Thanks for clarifying priorities. Marissa (product) and Laura (legal) are copied to provide an internal position and a pragmatic path forward. Quick outline of constraints from Redwood's side:

- We can grant ACME exclusive-enough rights to outputs for their productization (commercial use, sublicensing to end customers) when the outputs are generated solely from ACME inputs and prompts. However, we cannot assign ownership to the underlying model weights, model outputs derived from pre-trained Redwood models at large scale, or any Redwood-owned training artifacts.

- On training/data use: we accept opt-in training with explicit technical controls (time-bounded retention, differential access, anonymization) and a narrow license scope limited to improving model performance for ACME-specific workloads. We do not accept a perpetual unrestricted license by default.

Request for the legal/product teams: please propose precise redline language for the Order Form + an MSA carveout that ACME can accept without asking for blanket assignment. If possible, include a fall-through path (e.g., if ACME agrees to the opt-in training then Redwood will grant broader usage rights for outputs under a listed set of productization activities).

I want a concise recommendation we can send to Sarah and procurement today.

Thanks — Karthik

Folks —

Draft compromise below we think is reasonable and aligns with product constraints. Laura, this is my suggested plain-language summary to convert to redline text for the Order Form / MSA:

Option A (Recommended) — Scoped output title + opt-in training
- When outputs are generated solely from Customer-supplied inputs and prompts, Customer receives a perpetual, transferable license to use and sublicense those outputs for their business purposes, including commercial distribution to their customers. This license does not transfer title to Redwood preexisting models or model weights.
- Redwood will not use Customer content for model training or improvement unless Customer explicitly opts in via an Order Form checkbox and a separate Data Use Schedule. If Customer opts in, Redwood's license to use such content is limited to improving model performance for ACME's defined product lines, subject to retention and anonymization controls and a maximum 12-month usage period unless renewed.
- For telemetry and quality feedback, Redwood will provide aggregated usage metrics; any individual data needing deeper access will require Customer approval.

Option B — Stronger title ask (ACME asked for this)
- We would need direct business approvals and additional commercial consideration (higher fees) to accept assignment-like language. Also would require an SSO/enterprise-only routing model to isolate data for ACME's use.

Suggested next step: Laura to convert Option A into redline language (Order Form + Data Use Schedule) and share a marked PDF. Ben to send a one-page decision memo to ACME procurement summarizing Option A vs B and the commercial tradeoffs. If ACME picks Option A we can prepare a DocuSign-ready Order Form with the opt-in checkbox and Data Use Schedule.

Marissa
